issue_context.title: `BIT` type columns are not padded with left zeros
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```sql
drop table if exists tbl_3, tbl_23;
create table tbl_3 (col_15 bit(20));
insert into tbl_3 values (65535);
insert into tbl_3 values (255);
create table tbl_23 like tbl_3;
(select col_15 from tbl_23) union all (select col_15 from tbl_3 for update);
```

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

MySQL:
```
+----------------+
| col_15         |
+----------------+
| 0x00FFFF       |
| 0x0000FF       |
+----------------+
```

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

TiDB:
```
+----------------+
| col_15         |
+----------------+
| 0xFFFF         |
| 0xFF           |
+----------------+
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

master 
```
commit efc774aa5f9745359c5fe206aaafda768b1b0632 (upstream/master)
Author: ZhuoZhi <517770911@qq.com>
Date:   Wed Jun 16 15:12:37 2021 +0800

    planner: check filter condition in func convertToPartialTableScan (#25294)
```
comments:
This only happens in the special case:

```sql
(select col_15 from tbl_23) union all (select col_15 from tbl_3 for update); -- original case
+----------------+
| col_15         |
+----------------+
| 0xFFFF         |
| 0xFF           |
+----------------+
```

```sql
(select col_15 from tbl_23) union all (select col_15 from tbl_3); -- no 'FOR UPDATE'
+----------------+
| col_15         |
+----------------+
| 0x00FFFF       |
| 0x0000FF       |
+----------------+
```

```sql
select col_15 from tbl_3 for update; -- no 'UNION' operator
+----------------+
| col_15         |
+----------------+
| 0x00FFFF       |
| 0x0000FF       |
+----------------+
```

Problems like this fail AB tests between TiDB and MySQL.

review_comments: Could anyone explain to me why we use `byteSize := (ft.Flen + 7) >> 3` here?  I don't understand it.
And I find two other places using `(ft.Flen + 7) >> 3` also. Should we add a comment for it? Maybe there are people who don’t understand it, just like me.
In bit Type, Flen represents the number of bits, byteSize := (ft.Flen + 7) >> 3 is to convert the number of bits to the number of bytes.@mmyj
Thank you for your explain, and what is the effect of `(+7)>>3`?

`>> 3` is the same as dividing by 8,
`+7` is to prevent the number of bits that cannot be divisible by 8 causing the resulting bytes space is not enough to store the original data
for example if ft.Flen = 23，23/8 = 2, it's 16 bytes is not enough to store 20 bytes,but (23+7)/8 = 3,it's ok @mmyj
